h1: The 6 Best Conference Tables With Outlets for Hybrid Meetings, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Conference Tables With Outlets: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 conference tables with built-in outlets and USB ports for hybrid meetings, scored on power layout, top build and seating.
summary: The Anzhap 10-foot table is the best conference table with outlets, pairing built-in power and USB ports with patent-pending cable channels under a 2-inch top. The Oak and Grey 10-footer and the ZIMASYA share its footprint, the YITAHOME 94.5-inch is the value choice, and the OffiGo 79-inch is the one to pick if your team stands.
intro: Hybrid meetings changed what a conference table has to do. Every seat now carries a laptop, a phone and often a headset, so the power budget of a room is higher than it was ten years ago. A table that only has a cable hole in the middle forces everyone to share one strip and tangle the floor.

Six tables with outlets are ranked here. They are scored on how power is built in, how many people the table seats, the thickness and construction of the top, and whether cords are hidden. Tables that only gave a pop-up hub for a cutout were left out, since they are accessories, not tables.

products.name: Anzhap 10FT Conference Table with Power Outlets & USB, Oak & Gray
products.verdict: Built-in outlets and USB ports plus patent-pending cable channels under a 2-inch top.
products.description:
The Anzhap measures 118 by 51 by 30 inches, seats 10 and has built-in power outlets and USB ports. Its tabletop is 2 inches thick, and patent-pending cable channels run under the surface.

It places first because it solves both halves of the power problem: sockets at the table and a hidden path for the cords to reach the wall. Many tables give you one or the other. A 2-inch top spreads load across its length, so it does not dip when several laptops and a presenter's elbows lean on one end. The size is the cost, since a 10-foot table dominates any room under about 14 feet.

Buy it if you want power and tidy cables in one table. Skip it if your room is small.
pros: Outlets, USB and cable channels together
Oak and gray finish is neutral
products.idealFor: Boardrooms with a heavy device load.
products.skipIf: Your room is under 14 feet long.

products.name: 10ft Conference Table with Built-In Power Outlet, Oak and Grey
products.verdict: An integrated outlet rather than a cable hole, on a 118-inch table for ten.
products.description:
This 118 by 52 by 30 inch table seats 10 and has an integrated power outlet, which the listing distinguishes from simple cable routing. The top is 2 inches thick and rests on trapezoid metal legs.

It comes second because it is almost the same table as the Anzhap, minus the dedicated cable channels and the listed USB ports. The integrated outlet is the key phrase. A cable-routing hole only gives you a path for your own strip, while an integrated outlet gives you a socket in the table.

Buy it if you want integrated power with a thick top. Skip it if USB ports at the table matter to you.
pros: Integrated outlet, not just a hole
products.idealFor: Rooms that want sockets at the table.

products.name: ZIMASYA Conference Table with Power Outlets & USB, Walnut/Charcoal
products.verdict: A 118-inch walnut and charcoal table with built-in AC outlets and USB charging.
products.description:
The ZIMASYA is a 118 by 52 by 30 inch table with a 2-inch top in walnut and charcoal, with built-in AC outlets and USB charging ports. It is listed for medium-sized teams.

It ranks third because the listing is less specific on seating and on how cords are handled than the Anzhap. The dark finish suits formal offices and conceals fingerprints. The power layout is solid, with both AC and USB included.

Buy it if you want a formal dark table with USB at the seat. Skip it if you want a precise seating number.
pros: AC and USB both built in
products.skipIf: You want a stated seat count.

products.name: YITAHOME 94.5" Boat Shaped Conference Table with Power Outlets
products.verdict: A 94.5-inch boat table with 4 outlets, 2 USB ports and a 9.8 foot cord at a low price.
products.description:
The YITAHOME 94.5-inch is a boat-shaped table measuring 94.5 by 42.8 by 29.5 inches, seating 8 to 10, with 4 power outlets, 2 USB ports and a 9.8 foot cord. The top is P2 MDF with a scratch-resistant finish on a metal frame.

It lands fourth because it gives most of the power of the big tables at a fraction of the cost. The boat shape tapers at the ends so people can see each other down the length of the room. P2 MDF is lighter and thinner than the 2-inch tops above, which suits a team room rather than a client boardroom.

Buy it if you need power for eight to ten on a budget. Skip it if the table must impress clients.
pros: Lowest cost for eight to ten seats
Four outlets plus two USB ports
products.skipIf: You want a premium thick top.

products.name: OffiGo 79" Electric Standing Conference Desk, Rustic Brown
products.verdict: A height-adjustable 79-inch desk with 3 AC, 2 USB-A and 2 Type-C power points.
products.description:
The OffiGo is a 79 by 27.6 inch electric desk that adjusts from 29.1 to 48 inches, with 3 memory presets and a dual-beam frame. It also has 3 AC, 2 USB-A and 2 Type-C power points built in.

It ranks fifth because it is a working desk, not a meeting table: the top is only 27.6 inches deep, so people can sit along one side but not face each other. Where it shines is in power. Seven built-in points serve a small team, and height adjustment suits a mix of sitters and standers.

Buy it if your team works side by side and likes to stand. Skip it if you hold face-to-face meetings.
products.idealFor: Teams who stand and sit through the day.
products.skipIf: You want a table to meet around.

products.name: YITAHOME 70.8" Boat Shaped Conference Table with Power Outlets
products.verdict: A 70.8-inch boat table with 4 outlets and 2 USB ports for small meeting rooms.
products.description:
The small YITAHOME measures 70.8 by 35.43 by 29.5 inches, with 4 outlets, 2 USB ports and a 9.8 foot cord. The top is P2 MDF with a scratch-resistant finish on a metal frame.

It places sixth because the price bracket is higher than the bigger sibling, even though it seats fewer. The power layout is the same, though, and the footprint is easy to place in a small office or a huddle room.

Buy it if you have a small room and need powered seating for four to six. Skip it if you have the space for the larger YITAHOME.
pros: Four outlets and two USB ports
cons: Costs more than the larger YITAHOME
products.idealFor: Huddle rooms for four to six.
products.skipIf: You have room for the 94.5 inch.

whatMatters.detail: An integrated outlet is a socket in the table, while a routing hole only passes your own strip through. The Anzhap and the Oak and Grey table both advertise sockets. Look for words such as built-in or integrated.
USB ports let people charge phones without a brick, and Type-C ports handle modern laptops. The OffiGo has both Type-C and USB-A. Count the ports against your team size.
A channel under the top hides cords from the floor, which stops people tripping and keeps the room neat. The Anzhap lists patent-pending channels. Tables without them need adhesive clips.
A 2-inch top resists bowing over a 10-foot span. P2 MDF tops are lighter and cheaper. For a team that leans on the table all day, thickness is worth paying for.
The table plugs into a wall, so the cord must reach. The YITAHOME models list 9.8 feet. If your table sits in the room centre, plan for a floor cover or an in-floor box.

cards.text: Power at every seat, a camera-friendly layout and enough depth for a laptop plus a notebook.

cards.text: The Anzhap and ZIMASYA have the depth and power for hybrid use, while the boat-shaped YITAHOME helps remote viewers see faces.

faq.q: Do the outlets work out of the box?
faq.a: They plug into a wall outlet with the supplied cord, so no wiring is needed. The YITAHOME lists a 9.8 foot cord. Make sure the wall outlet is within reach.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying one?
faq.a: Assuming a cable hole means outlets. Only tables that list built-in or integrated outlets have sockets. Check the product page.

faq.q: Is the Anzhap worth it over the YITAHOME?
faq.a: For a client-facing room, yes, thanks to the thick top and cable channels. For an internal room, the YITAHOME gives power at a much lower price.
Allow one to two hours with two or three people for the 10-foot tables. Attach the legs, set the top, then connect the cord.

faq.q: Is a standing desk a good meeting table?
faq.a: It works for side-by-side working sessions, not facing meetings. The 27.6 inch depth is the limit.
A surge-protected strip under the table works. The Anzhap's cable channels make routing simple.

finalTake: The Anzhap 10-foot table is the best conference table with outlets, giving you built-in power, USB ports and cable channels under a 2-inch top. The Oak and Grey and ZIMASYA tables are close alternatives, and the YITAHOME 94.5-inch is the value choice for a team room. Choose the OffiGo only if your team stands. Confirm the outlets are built in before you order.
